section_1.title: The 'Why': Explicit vs. Implicit
section_1.content: Briefly review explicit functions (y = f(x)) where y is isolated. Introduce the limitation: many curves (like circles or hearts) cannot be written as a single function of y. Use an animation showing a circle x² + y² = r² and explaining we need a way to find the slope (dy/dx) even when y is 'trapped'.
section_1.example: Comparing y = x² (Easy) vs. x² + y² = 25 (The 'trapped' y).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Core
section_2.content: Recall the Chain Rule: d/dx [f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x). Emphasize that whenever we differentiate a term containing 'y' with respect to 'x', we must treat 'y' as an inner function and multiply by dy/dx.
section_2.example: Visualizing d/dx [y²] as 2y * (dy/dx) using a 'shadow' operator metaphor.

section_3.title: The Step-by-Step Algorithm
section_3.content: Present the 3-step process: 1. Differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to x. 2. Group all dy/dx terms on one side. 3. Factor out dy/dx and solve. Use a 'Robot Assembly Line' animation to show terms being processed.
section_3.example: Differentiating x³ + y³ = 6xy (The Folium of Descartes).

section_4.title: Application: The Geometry of a Bouncing Ball
section_4.content: Demonstrate the power of the technique. Find the slope of the tangent line to a complex path at a specific point. This shows the practical utility of finding velocity/slope when a coordinate is defined implicitly.
section_4.example: A cat running along a figure-eight path: finding the exact direction the cat is heading at a specific coordinate.

section_5.title: Summary & Quick Check
section_5.content: Review the 'Chain Rule' requirement. Provide a final 'Don't Forget' tip: Always verify that the dy/dx is present whenever a 'y' term is differentiated. Flash a summary slide.
section_5.example: Quick fire: What is d/dx [sin(y)]? Answer: cos(y) * dy/dx.

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Geometry of a Bouncing Ball", 
                          ["We apply this to complex paths.", 
                           "Find tangent slopes for any point.", 
                           "Easily determine velocity on any curve."])
        
        # --- Elements ---
        equation = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 = r^2", color="#FFFFFF")
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#00FF00")
        ball = Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.15)
        tangent_line = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color="#FFD700")
        
        # Initial positions
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # --- Animation ---
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.add(ball)
        ball.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(self.time * 2)))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(tangent_line, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(tangent_line)
        
        def update_tangent(mob):
            angle = self.time * 2
            point = circle.point_at_angle(angle)
            mob.move_to(point)
            # Tangent is perpendicular to radius vector (angle + PI/2)
            mob.set_angle(angle + PI/2)
        
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Cleanup
        ball.remove_updater(None)
        tangent_line.remove_updater(None)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Geometry of a Bouncing Ball", 
                          ["We apply this to complex paths.", 
                           "Find tangent slopes for any point.", 
                           "Easily determine velocity on any curve."])
        
        # --- Elements ---
        equation = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 = r^2", color="#FFFFFF")
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#00FF00")
        ball = Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.15)
        tangent_line = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color="#FFD700")
        
        # Initial positions
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # --- Animation ---
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.add(ball)
        ball.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(self.time * 2)))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(tangent_line, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(tangent_line)
        
        def update_tangent(mob):
            angle = self.time * 2
            point = circle.point_at_angle(angle)
            mob.move_to(point)
            # Tangent is perpendicular to radius vector (angle + PI/2)
            mob.set_angle(angle + PI/2)
        
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Cleanup
        ball.remove_updater(None)
        tangent_line.remove_updater(None)
